alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.subtitle: Define rules and review recent events
alerts.no_rules: No rules yet. Click "New rule" to create one.
alerts.toggle_webhook_hint:
Forward this rule's events to the configured webhook (Settings → Exports → Webhook).

When the rule fires or resolves, GpuViewR POSTs:
• rule_name, metric, threshold, observed value
• gpu_index, state (firing/resolved), message
• triggered_at (epoch) + ISO timestamp

Discord/Telegram payloads are reformatted automatically. Toggle OFF here to keep the alert local (browser/sound only).
alerts.webhook_active_hint:
Webhook ON for this rule.
On firing/resolving, an HTTP POST is sent to the webhook configured in Settings → Exports.
Payload: rule_name, metric, threshold, observed, gpu_index, state, message, triggered_at.
alerts.webhook_inactive_hint: Webhook OFF for this rule. Browser/sound notifications still fire, but no HTTP request is sent.
alerts.presets_help: Pick the classic GPU alerts you want to add. They land disabled so you can tweak thresholds before arming them.
alerts.presets_disabled_note: Added rules start disabled — review and enable each one.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Personalize the dashboard
settings.chart_palette_help: Pick a preset palette or fine-tune each metric's color individually. The gradient area fill underneath the line follows the selected color.
settings.about_description: GpuViewR streams live GPU metrics over WebSocket, stores history in SQLite, fires alerts, and exports to Prometheus, MQTT (with Home Assistant discovery), InfluxDB v2 and webhooks. Packaged as a single multi-arch Docker image.
settings.about_banner_help: Show a banner on the dashboard when a new release is available. Disable to hide it permanently.
settings.gauge_view_help: Switch between arc gauges and Grafana-style horizontal bars.
settings.lang_more_help: More languages can be added under src/i18n/locales/.
settings.thresholds_help: Display dashed reference lines on the live chart for each metric. Leave a field empty to disable that line.
settings.db_retention_help: Samples older than this are pruned automatically every hour.
settings.db_purge_all_confirm: Wipe ALL GPU history? This cannot be undone.
settings.exports_help: Forward GPU samples to external systems. Each exporter can be enabled independently.
settings.exports_mqtt_help: Publishes one retained JSON message per GPU on <prefix>/gpu<N>/state. With HA discovery enabled, sensors auto-appear in Home Assistant.
settings.exports_webhook_headers_empty: No custom headers. Add one to send things like Authorization or X-API-Key with each request.
settings.exports_webhook_fields_help: Select which keys go into each sample object. Discord/Telegram payloads are reformatted server-side and ignore this list.
settings.notifications_help: Global preferences applied to every alert that fires. Per-rule sound and browser flags on the Alerts page only take effect if these are enabled here.
settings.browser_notifs_denied_help: Unblock GpuViewR in your browser's site settings to receive notifications.
settings.exports_ha_help_title: How to set this up on Home Assistant
settings.exports_ha_help_intro: GpuViewR publishes one retained MQTT message per GPU and (optionally) Home Assistant discovery topics, so each GPU appears as a device with sensors. Configure the broker on the HA side first, then point the form above at it.
exports_ha_help_steps: Install an MQTT broker reachable by both Home Assistant and GpuViewR. The simplest path is the Mosquitto broker add-on (Settings → Add-ons → Add-on Store → 'Mosquitto broker' → Install → Start).
Create an MQTT user for GpuViewR (Settings → People → Users → Add user). Give it a username and password — this is what you fill in the Username / Password fields above.

Add the MQTT integration in HA (Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → MQTT). Enter the broker host (use 'core-mosquitto' if the add-on runs on the same HA instance, otherwise the broker IP), port 1883, and the user/password from step 2.

Back in this page, set Broker URL to mqtt://<broker-host>:1883, fill the same Username / Password, leave Topic prefix as 'gpuviewr' (or change it — it must not collide with another device), enable HA discovery, then Save and click 'Send test'.

Within ~10 seconds, sensors appear in HA under Settings → Devices & services → MQTT → 'GpuViewR GPU 0' (one device per GPU). Each device exposes utilization, temperature, memory, power, fan and clocks as separate entities you can graph or trigger automations on.
settings.exports_ha_help_note: If sensors don't appear, check the 'What's being sent' panel above for the resolved state/discovery topics, and verify the broker is reachable from both sides (HA → MQTT integration shows 'Connected', GpuViewR → 'Send test' returns success).
settings.exports_webhook_mode_alerts_help: The webhook fires whenever an alert rule transitions to firing or resolved (event-driven).
settings.exports_webhook_mode_metrics_help: The webhook posts the latest GPU samples on a fixed interval (data sink mode).
settings.updates_frequency_help: How often the server polls GitHub for new releases. The result is cached for this duration.
